transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE); Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE); Jin Park (BlueWave, Head of ML); Marta Gomez (BlueWave, Infra); Liam Chen (BlueWave, CTO)

Summary:
Quick weekly sync on the ongoing pilot focused on throughput optimizations - continuous batching, concurrency targets, queue sizing. Reviewed last week's run (steady-state 120 QPS, p95 ~620ms), discussed tuning steps and next benchmark to target p95 under 500ms with minimal cost increase. Agreed on config changes to test and owners for artifacts.

Topics:
- Last run results and anomalies
- Continuous batching parameters and side effects
- Concurrency targets vs queueing latency
- Autoscaling and prefill/backpressure settings
- Next benchmark and deliverables

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining for the weekly sync, hope that time still works for you, quick check in before we jump into the numbers?
[00:05] Jin: yes thanks, still good. we ran the traffic window like we discussed last week, we hit averages around a hundred to 125 qps with some spikes to 160 for a few minutes, overall p50 looks good p95 was around six-twenty which we want to bring down.
[00:18] Ethan: ok great thank you, i pulled the trace logs this morning. side note, the kv cache hit rate is about 38% for the common prefixes which is lower than expected given prompt overlap, so we're not getting as much prefix cache benefit.
[00:30] Marta: that matches what we saw in infra, cache locality is a bit fragmented across hosts because your traffic is spread and we have some sticky sessions disabled for the pilot.
[00:40] Ethan: got it. first main area is continuous batching tuning. current policy is max_batch_size 64, batch_timeout_ms 12, and target_concurrency 8 per GPU slot — that's giving us good throughput but the tail is hurting.
[00:55] Jin: can you explain the tradeoff again between increasing target_concurrency vs increasing max_batch_size?
[01:02] Ethan: sure, increasing max_batch_size raises per-batch efficiency (more tokens/batch -> lower cost per token) but it also increases the time an individual request waits for the batch to fill, which raises p95 latency. increasing target_concurrency allows more requests to be processed in parallel by creating more in-flight micro-batches, lowering queue wait time at the cost of slightly higher GPU memory usage and potential kv cache fragmentation. continuous batching tries to find the sweet spot by dynamically forming batches under latency SLOs.
[01:35] Liam: so what's your suggestion for our workload where we have short prompts mostly and occasional multi-turn spikes?
[01:41] Ethan: for short prompt workloads with bursty spikes we usually recommend lowering batch_timeout_ms to 6-8 ms, keep max_batch_size around 48, and raise target_concurrency to 12-16 for the pilot's dedicated slot. that reduces p95 without sacrificing too much throughput efficiency.
[02:00] Samira: we also should consider small queueing backpressure - a bounded queue length per slot like 200 requests and drop-to-fallback policy if queue saturates, that keeps latency predictable.
[02:12] Marta: is dropping acceptable for our use case? we need to avoid user-facing errors; maybe we prefer graceful queuing with a short retry/backoff to the hosted fallback.
[02:20] Samira: yes we can configure fallback to hosted Redwood API for excess traffic or redirect to a cheaper variant of the model with faster decode — automatic fallback is in the pilot config we can enable.
[02:32] Jin: last time we saw a long tail caused by cold KV cache misses after a scale event, any suggestions?
[02:38] Ethan: two approaches: prefill KV cache for the hottest prefixes during scale-up and use warmup traffic to populate caches; or use sticky routing for short windows to preserve cache locality. both have tradeoffs — prefill costs tokens but reduces p95; sticky routing can cause imbalance.
[02:55] Liam: can the platform show per-prefix hitrate so we can pick top-10 prefixes to prefill?
[03:00] Ethan: yes we'll export a hitrate report, i'll include top prefixes and a recommendation for warmup script.
[03:10] Jin: what about autoscaling policy settings? we want to avoid oscillation but also not to underprovision.
[03:16] Ethan: set autoscale cooldown to 90s, scale-step min 1 gpu up to 2, and use a combination of sustained QPS and p95 > threshold triggers. also set a conservative min capacity to handle 95th of expected traffic.
[03:30] Samira: ok let's look at the numbers from last run i shared — (shows spreadsheet link) p50 110ms p90 280ms p95 620ms average batch size 36, concurrency per slot hovered 7.
[03:45] Jin: average batch size 36, interesting given max was 64 — that indicates not enough requests to fill large batches before timeout.
[03:52] Ethan: exactly. another lever is adaptive batching that grows batch size based on rolling qps window; we can enable that so batch target increases during spikes without bumping timeout.
[04:05] Marta: enable adaptive but cap at 48?
[04:08] Ethan: yep cap at 48 is reasonable. also enable per-request priority tagging so interactive requests have a small fast-path queue.
[04:18] Jin: how do we measure cost impact of these changes? we want to keep per-token cost within 5% of current baseline while improving p95.
[04:24] Samira: we'll run a controlled A/B with identical traffic and compare token counts, GPU-hours and latency. Ethan will provide the config and scripts to reproduce.
[04:32] Ethan: i'll share a benchmark harness and a script that replays traffic with the same QPS distribution and spike pattern. it'll produce CSVs with throughput, p50/p90/p95, avg batch size, cache hitrate.
[04:45] Liam: for the next benchmark what are the explicit targets?
[04:48] Samira: target p95 under 500ms, p90 under 300ms, maintain throughput within 90-100% of baseline cost.
[04:56] Jin: timeline?
[04:58] Samira: we want the new benchmark run by 2026-03-25 and then another sync to review results 2026-03-26 or 27.
[05:06] Marta: one more infra note — our network egress to the Redwood Dedicated cluster in the eu-west region had a few 5xx spikes during the last test, we should include region health in the next run.
[05:15] Ethan: noted. we'll split runs regionally and tag metrics.
[05:20] Jin: any quick wins we can apply now?
[05:22] Ethan: yes, quick wins: lower batch_timeout to 8ms, cap adaptive batch size at 48, bump target_concurrency to 12, enable prioritized fast-path for interactive, enable warmup prefill for top-10 prefixes. these are low-risk and reversible.
[05:35] Samira: sounds good. Samira to follow up on pricing nuance for temporary spike capacity and credits if you need Dedicated trial.
[05:44] Liam: ok great thanks, that feels actionable.
[05:48] Samira: recap of next steps and owners — we listed them, any final q's?
[05:52] Jin: none from me.
[05:53] Marta: none.
[05:54] Samira: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts and schedule the deep dive.

End of transcript.
